title: Star Trek
subtitle: every episode and all thirteen films, in production order
blurb: Sixty years of it in the order it was made — 961 episodes across twelve series, with the thirteen films sitting beside the crews they belong to.
notes: The films sit with the crew they belong to.

Each block of films follows the series whose cast it continues, at the point those films begin: the six original-cast films after the animated series, the four Next Generation films immediately after that show's finale, and the three Kelvin films in the gap after Enterprise when nothing was being made for television. Six of the thirteen came out while some series was in its run, and the section headings say so.
Series run in the order they premiered.

Which is why Lower Decks and Prodigy sit ahead of Strange New Worlds — they started first. Nine of the twelve series were on the air at the same time as another one, so no arrangement of whole series is strictly chronological; premiere date is the rule this page keeps to.
One section per season, running series by series, each headed with the series it belongs to. The alternative was a single 178-row accordion for The Next Generation with no season markers in it.
Twenty-three rows cover two episodes each.

Wikipedia's episode tables file some two-part stories as one row and this list follows them, carrying both numbers. Seventeen of those went out as a single installment and six a week apart; every one of the rows says which. That is 938 rows covering 961 episodes.

The thirteen films' runtimes are known — Wikidata carries all thirteen, about 26 hours, and the film headings add them up. The episodes are not so lucky: of 938 episode rows, 685 carry a runtime on Wikidata and 253 carry nothing, and the gap is not random — the classic shows are nearly covered while Picard, Lower Decks and Prodigy have not one runtime between them. A weighted list counts a row with no weight as one hour, so weighting what is known would push a guessed hour into every finish date 253 times over. An episode and a film each count one.
The Cage rides along, marked optional.
The 1964 pilot is not one of the 79 original-series episodes and was not broadcast until 1988, so it sits in a section of its own above season one.
What is not on this page.

Star Trek: Section 31 is a television film rather than one of the thirteen theatrical features, and the Short Treks are not episodes of any of these series. Strange New Worlds' fifth season has been ordered but has no announced titles or dates, so it has no rows yet. Starfleet Academy's second and final season is due in March 2027 with no titles announced, so for now it is one row, its premiere.

Titles, numbering and broadcast dates machine-read from Wikipedia's per-series episode tables; every season's enumerated rows are asserted against that article's own Series overview count before this builds. Film runtimes and release dates from Wikidata, gated on a matching release year.
